learning_objective: 🎯 Welcome to Practical Geography! Learn what data is, where to find it, and how to gather the numbers that tell geographical stories.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Information in the form of numbers or facts that are collected to be analyzed. In geography, data is needed to understand patterns like rainfall, population, or crop yield.
Data collected firsthand by the researcher for a specific purpose. Collected through personal interviews, questionnaires, observations, or field measurements.
Data that already exists and was collected by someone else. Examples include government reports, Census of India, newspapers, and international publications.
A tool for collecting primary data. Good questionnaires are short, simple, logical, and respect the privacy of the respondent.
Raw data is a mess. Compilation means organizing it into tallies and classes (like 0-10, 10-20). Tabulation means presenting this organized data neatly in rows and columns.

fun_activity.title: 📋 The Mini Census
fun_activity.instructions: Create a 3-question survey (e.g., 'What is your favorite subject?'). Ask 10 classmates and record their answers. You just collected and compiled Primary Data!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between Primary data (original, time-consuming) and Secondary data (existing, quick but maybe outdated).
📌 Know the essential rules for designing a good questionnaire.
📌 Understand the difference between absolute data (total population) and derived data (density, percentages).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Census of India, conducted every 10 years, is the largest source of secondary demographic data in India.
⭐ Unstructured interviews allow for open discussions, while structured interviews follow strict questionnaires.
⭐ Tabulation makes large amounts of raw data easy to read and compare.
